name: SkyDB
tagline: Ben Johnson's 2012-2013 open-source database for behavioral (clickstream and event) analytics.
description: Sky stored per-object timelines of events, where each object (typically a user) carried permanent properties such as country and transient ones such as the action taken at a moment. Its query engine walked each timeline in order, which made funnels, session splitting and next-action analysis a fast sequential scan instead of the self-joins they need in SQL. Version 0.3.0 (April 2013) rewrote about 95% of the code in Go, stored MessagePack-encoded data in LevelDB, compiled queries with LuaJIT and exposed a JSON-over-HTTP API. Development stopped soon after; the author went on to write BoltDB. Today it is only a design reference, and event analytics belongs in a columnar engine.
statusNote: Development stopped after v0.3.0 (April 2013); the original skydb/sky repo and skydb.io site are gone. Use ClickHouse, Apache Pinot or Druid for event analytics.

scale.notes: Single server; distributed execution was planned for a later release that never shipped publicly.

strengths: Per-object event timelines turn funnel and next-step queries into a single ordered scan
Permanent vs transient property model is a clean way to describe behavioral data
Reported millions of events per core per second on commodity hardware
weaknesses: Single node only, no clustering or replication
No SQL, joins or secondary indexes
Original repository deleted; only forks remain
useCases: Historical reference for behavioral database design
